name: ziplark-mcp
description: Read and write archives — ZIP, RAR (incl. multi-volume), 7z, tar, ISO — from an MCP client.
long_description: Ziplark's archive engine over the Model Context Protocol. Lists, extracts, verifies and creates archives: ZIP, RAR and RAR5 (including multi-volume sets, encrypted headers and self-extracting archives), 7z, tar and the compressed-tar variants, single-stream gz/bz2/xz/zst/lz4, and ISO 9660 / Joliet disc images. Listings are paged, so a 200,000-entry archive costs the same context as a small one, and entries can be extracted by exact path rather than by substring. Every extraction path is funnelled through a single guard, so no entry can be written outside the destination directory. Read tools are always available; extracting and creating require --allow-write.

tools.name: ziplark_info
tools.description: What kind of archive this is and what shape it is in: format, entry count, sizes, encryption, and — for a RAR set — its volumes, whether one is missing, whether it is solid, and its comment.

tools.name: ziplark_list
tools.description: List the entries inside an archive, paged, with per-directory counts when the result is truncated.

tools.name: ziplark_test
tools.description: Verify archive integrity by decompressing every entry. Writes nothing, and reports every bad entry rather than the first.

tools.name: ziplark_extract
tools.description: Extract an archive, or exactly the entries named, into a destination directory. Requires --allow-write.

tools.name: ziplark_create
tools.description: Create a ZIP (AES-256), 7z (AES-256) or tar archive from files and directories. Requires --allow-write.
